nodes.name: Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: Let $k = 2r$ be a positive even integer and $F$ be an infinite field whose characteristic does not divide $2(2r+1)r!$. Assume that $n > r$. Then for $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_k\in {\rm Mat}_n(F)$ in general position, the nullity of $L(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_k)$ is $k$.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement:
Assume that $k = 2r$ is even, $n > r$, the base field $F$ is infinite of characteristic not dividing $2(2r+1)r!$, and
the matrices $A_1, \ldots, A_k$ are as in~(3.3). Let $L_j \colon V_j \to V_{j + s_1 + \ldots + s_k}$ 
be the restriction of $L(A_1, \ldots, A_k)$ to $V_j$. Then for some choice of the exponents $s_1, \ldots, s_k \in {\mathbb Z}$, 
\[ {\rm null}(L_0)+\dots+{\rm null}(L_{n-1})\leqslant k. \]

nodes.name: Proposition 6.3
nodes.statement:
Assume that $n>r$ and that the base field $F$ is infinite of characteristic not dividing $r!$.

\smallskip
(a) If $j \neq 0$ then \[ {\rm null} ({\rm Ic}(L_j))\leqslant \delta_j, \]
where
\[ \delta_j = \begin{cases} \text{$2$, if both $j$ and $-j$ lie in $[\lceil r/2 \rceil \longleftrightarrow \lfloor r/2 \rfloor]$, } \\
\text{$1$, if exactly one of $j, -j$ lies in $[\lceil r/2 \rceil \longleftrightarrow \lfloor r/2 \rfloor]$,} \\
\text{$0$, if neither $j$ nor $-j$ lie in $[\lceil r/2 \rceil \longleftrightarrow \lfloor r/2 \rfloor]$.}
\end{cases}
\]

\smallskip
(b) Assume further that the characteristic of $F$ does not divide $2(2r+1)r!$. Then the $n \times n$ matrix ${\rm Ic}(L_0)$ is non-singular.

Proposition 9.1, Section 10
nodes.statement:
Let $1 \leqslant r < n$, $a, j \in \mathbb Z / n \mathbb Z$ and $j \neq 0$. Assume that $F$ is an infinite field of characteristic not dividing
$r!$. If both $a$ and $a+j$ lie in ${\rm supp}(H_r) = [-\lceil r/2 \rceil\longleftrightarrow \lfloor r/2 \rfloor]$, assume further that $a, a+j \neq 0$. Then
\[ \text{$({\rm Ic}(L_j))_{a,b}= 0$ for any $b\neq a$ and
$({\rm Ic}(L_j))_{a,a}\neq 0$} \]
in $F$.

nodes.name: Lemma 8.1, Lemma 8.2
nodes.statement:
Assume $n>r$. There exists $G\in U(a,j)$ containing $H_t$ (for $t>0$) if and only if $R_t(a)\cap {\rm supp}(H_t)\neq\emptyset$.

Let $0\leqslant t\leqslant r$ be the largest integer such that there exists $G\in U(a,j)$ containing $H_t$. Set $s=\sum_{i\in I_t^+}s_i$. Then

\smallskip
(a) $s\leqslant |a|, |a+j|$.

\smallskip
(b) If $t>0$ and $v\in R_t(a)\cap {\rm supp}(H_t)$ then either every $s_i$ for $i \in I_t^+$ or every $s_i$ for $i \in I_t^-$  
must appear as a summand of $v$.
